deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page continues Riemann's list of the Newtonian hypotheses behind falling motion and planetary motion. It then states his own hypothesis about the cause of gravity. The text belongs to the fragment 'Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie' (dated 1853; printed in the Nachlass section of the Gesammelte Werke, 1876).

I. Law of the accelerating force produced by the ponderable points.

(1) Single mass point. Suppose a single ponderable point is at x_0. The force field at x is then directed toward x_0, with magnitude |F| = mu/r^2, where r = |x - x_0|. In vector form F(x) = -mu (x - x_0)/r^3. The product |F| r^2 = mu is the same at every point of space and is given a name. The underlined word is uncertain; it is the point's gravitational strength, called 'Anziehungskraft' on p. 35.

(2) Superposition. The force actually present is the vector (parallelogram) sum over all points: F(x) = -sum_i mu_i (x - x_i)/|x - x_i|^3.

(3) The force is a field property of the place, not of the body.
- A cause at each point of space would give every ponderable point resting there the same motion, whatever its mass. So it is an acceleration field, a weak-equivalence-type statement.
- A point already moving combines its existing velocity with the velocity a resting point would acquire, by the parallelogram rule: v(t+dt) = v(t) + F dt.
- Hence these causes differ in magnitude and direction. Measured by the motion they impart, they are 'beschleunigende Kräfte' (Newton's 'vis acceleratrix', Principia Def. VII).

II. Riemann's ether hypothesis.
- The cause of the accelerating force at a place is sought in the state of motion of a substance (Stoff) that continuously fills all of infinite space.
- The velocity of this substance has the direction of the force (or the opposite) and speed proportional to its magnitude: u(x,t) = ±c F(x,t).
- Margin note: the substance forms a 'physical space' whose points move within geometric space. These are motions in the space free of ponderable bodies.

Consequence for one resting point mass (the sentence completed on p. 35): the substance streams radially from all sides toward the point. Its speed is proportional to mu/r^2: u = -c mu (x - x_0)/r^3.

Implicit step (mine), which justifies p. 35's 'es lässt sich leicht zeigen':
- div u = 0 for r > 0, so the flow is incompressible: the same quantity of Stoff always occupies the same volume.
- The flux through any sphere around x_0 is -4 pi c mu, independent of the radius.
- So the point must act as a sink, swallowing 4 pi c mu of substance per unit time, proportional to its attractive strength (p. 35).
- By linearity, the superposed field of many points is also divergence-free away from the masses.
errors: No mathematical errors on the page.

Conceptual: the ether's velocity is made proportional to the force itself, not its time integral. The Stoff therefore has no inertia, which p. 35 states explicitly. The field is also assumed to follow the instantaneous mass configuration, so there is no propagation delay in the gravitational part.

The equivalence-type statement in (3), that the same acceleration holds for all masses, is posited as a hypothesis rather than derived. The previous page defines mass via force/acceleration, which overlaps with this somewhat circularly.
Numbering inconsistency carried over from the previous page (two items labelled 4).

results.what: Newtonian axioms restated: inverse-square central force, vector superposition, force as an acceleration field independent of the test mass, parallelogram composition of velocities
results.modern_name: Newtonian gravitational field / superposition / weak equivalence principle

results.what: Gravity explained by a continuous space-filling medium whose velocity field is proportional to the gravitational field; masses act as sinks of the incompressible flow
results.modern_name: ether-sink (fluid-sink) theory of gravitation; analogue of Gauss's law / divergence-free flow
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1853 (published posthumously 1876); related sink models by Bjerknes, Pearson and others later

deep.surprise_reason: This is the known fragment 'Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie', printed in Riemann's Werke (1876) and discussed in the literature on his ether theory of gravitation. The mathematics is elementary (inverse-square field, divergence-free radial flow).

checkable.asserts: The radial inflow u = -x/r^3 is divergence-free away from the origin (incompressible, as claimed on p.35)
Flux through a sphere of radius R equals -4*pi*c*mu, independent of R, so the point mass swallows Stoff at a constant rate proportional to mu
Force times squared distance is constant for an inverse-square field

transcription_corrections: The underlined word at the end of law 1 ('seine Schwere[?]') is uncertain from the image. The defined quantity corresponds to what p. 35 calls the point's 'Anziehungskraft' (attractive strength).
Margin note: 'physischen Raum' is plausible (cf. 'physische Raumelement' on p. 35).
'virium quantitates acceleratrices' is split across lines as 'accele/ratrices' in the manuscript.
